development.title: Calantha Interactive Platform
development.description: Full-stack web application with real-time video processing and interactive media features.
development.longDescription:
Calantha is a comprehensive interactive media platform that combines real-time video processing with social features. Built using modern web technologies, it provides users with tools to create, edit, and share multimedia content seamlessly.

The platform features a microservices architecture with separate services for user management, media processing, real-time communication, and content delivery. The frontend is built with React and TypeScript, providing a responsive and intuitive user interface.

Key technical achievements include implementing WebRTC for real-time video communication, optimizing media processing pipelines, and creating a scalable backend infrastructure capable of handling thousands of concurrent users.
features: Interactive media processing and editing tools
Social features including comments and sharing
Responsive design optimized for all devices
challenges: Implementing efficient real-time video streaming
Optimizing media processing for various file formats
Scaling WebSocket connections for thousands of users
Managing real-time state synchronization across multiple clients
Ensuring cross-browser compatibility for WebRTC features

development.title: NextGen E-commerce Platform
development.description: Full-featured e-commerce platform with advanced analytics, inventory management, and payment processing.
development.longDescription:
NextGen E-commerce is a comprehensive online shopping platform built with modern technologies and scalable architecture. The platform handles everything from product catalog management to order fulfillment, featuring real-time inventory tracking, advanced search capabilities, and integrated payment processing.

The system is designed with microservices architecture, ensuring high availability and scalability. It includes a robust admin dashboard for merchants, advanced analytics for business intelligence, and a seamless shopping experience for customers across all devices.

Key features include multi-vendor support, subscription-based products, advanced product filtering, personalized recommendations using machine learning, and comprehensive order management system.
challenges: Implementing complex inventory tracking across multiple vendors
Ensuring PCI DSS compliance for payment processing
Optimizing search performance for large product catalogs
Managing real-time stock updates across multiple channels
Creating responsive design for complex e-commerce interfaces

development.title: Enterprise Cloud Infrastructure
development.description: Scalable cloud architecture with Docker, Kubernetes, and automated CI/CD pipelines for enterprise applications.
development.longDescription:
Enterprise Cloud Infrastructure is a comprehensive DevOps solution designed for high-availability applications. Built using Infrastructure as Code principles, it provides automated deployment, scaling, and monitoring capabilities for modern web applications.

The infrastructure leverages AWS services with Terraform for provisioning, Kubernetes for orchestration, and GitLab CI/CD for automated deployments. It includes monitoring with Prometheus and Grafana, logging with ELK stack, and security scanning integrated into the pipeline.

This project demonstrates expertise in cloud-native technologies, security best practices, and operational excellence in managing production-grade applications.
challenges: Designing highly available multi-AZ architecture
Implementing zero-downtime deployment strategies
Managing Kubernetes cluster security and RBAC
Optimizing costs while maintaining performance
Ensuring compliance with enterprise security policies

development.title: RESTful API Gateway Service
development.description: High-performance API gateway with GraphQL integration, rate limiting, and comprehensive authentication system.
development.longDescription:
The RESTful API Gateway Service is a robust backend solution designed to handle high-traffic mobile and web applications. Built with FastAPI and Python, it provides a unified interface for multiple microservices while ensuring security, performance, and scalability.

The service includes advanced features like intelligent rate limiting, API versioning, comprehensive logging, and real-time monitoring. It supports multiple authentication methods, including JWT, OAuth2, and API keys, with role-based access control.

GraphQL integration allows for flexible data querying, while Redis caching ensures optimal performance. The API is fully documented with OpenAPI/Swagger and includes automated testing and deployment pipelines.
features: RESTful API design with OpenAPI documentation
GraphQL endpoint for flexible data queries
challenges: Implementing efficient caching strategies for complex queries
Designing flexible rate limiting for different user tiers
Ensuring API security against common vulnerabilities
Optimizing database queries for high concurrency
Managing API versioning without breaking existing clients

design.title: Zena Fashion Brand Identity
design.description: Complete brand identity design including logo, typography, and visual system.
design.longDescription:
Zena Fashion needed a sophisticated brand identity that would appeal to young professionals while communicating their commitment to sustainable fashion. The challenge was to create a visual system that felt both modern and timeless, luxury yet accessible.

The solution involved developing a minimalist logo that could work across all mediums, from tiny social media avatars to large-scale storefront signage. The typography system combines a elegant serif for headlines with a clean sans-serif for body text, creating a perfect balance between sophistication and readability.

thoughtProcess.problem: Zena Fashion needed a sophisticated brand identity that would appeal to young professionals while communicating their commitment to sustainable fashion. The existing brand lacked cohesion and failed to differentiate from competitors.
thoughtProcess.solution: Developed a minimalist yet elegant brand identity system featuring a custom logotype, earthy color palette, and sophisticated typography that reflects both modernity and sustainability values.
thoughtProcess.approach: Started with extensive market research and competitor analysis. Created mood boards and brand personas. Developed multiple logo concepts and tested them across various applications. Refined the chosen direction based on stakeholder feedback.
thoughtProcess.outcome: The new brand identity successfully positioned Zena as a premium sustainable fashion brand. Brand recognition increased by 85% and social media engagement improved by 120% within the first quarter after launch.

achievements: Won 'Best Brand Identity' at 2024 Design Awards

cloud-infrastructure.code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web-application
  namespace: production
  labels:
    app: web-application
    version: v1.0.0
spec:
  replicas: 3
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 1
      maxUnavailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web-application
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web-application
        version: v1.0.0
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: web-application
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 1000
        fsGroup: 1000
      containers:
      - name: web-app
        image: myregistry/web-application:v1.0.0
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
          name: http
          protocol: TCP
        env:
        - name: NODE_ENV
          value: "production"
        - name: PORT
          value: "3000"
        - name: DB_HOST
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: database-credentials
              key: host
        - name: DB_PASSWORD
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: database-credentials
              key: password
        resources:
          requests:
            memory: "256Mi"
            cpu: "250m"
          limits:
            memory: "512Mi"
            cpu: "500m"
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: http
          initialDelaySeconds: 30
          periodSeconds: 10
          timeoutSeconds: 5
          successThreshold: 1
          failureThreshold: 3
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: http
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 5
          timeoutSeconds: 3
          successThreshold: 1
          failureThreshold: 3
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config-volume
          mountPath: /app/config
          readOnly: true
      volumes:
      - name: config-volume
        configMap:
          name: web-application-config
      imagePullSecrets:
      - name: registry-secret
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: web-application-service
  namespace: production
  labels:
    app: web-application
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
    protocol: TCP
    name: http
  selector:
    app: web-application

#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

# Configuration
REGION="us-west-2"
CLUSTER_NAME="production-cluster"
NAMESPACE="production"
IMAGE_TAG="${GITHUB_SHA:-latest}"
REGISTRY="123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com"
APP_NAME="web-application"

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

log() {
    echo -e "${GREEN}[$(date +'%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] $1${NC}"
}

warn() {
    echo -e "${YELLOW}[$(date +'%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] WARNING: $1${NC}"
}

error() {
    echo -e "${RED}[$(date +'%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] ERROR: $1${NC}"
}

# Check required tools
check_dependencies() {
    log "Checking dependencies..."
    
    for cmd in docker aws kubectl helm; do
        if ! command -v $cmd &> /dev/null; then
            error "$cmd is not installed or not in PATH"
            exit 1
        fi
    done
    
    log "All dependencies are available"
}

# Build and push Docker image
build_and_push() {
    log "Building Docker image..."
    
    # Build the image
    docker build -t $APP_NAME:$IMAGE_TAG .
    
    # Tag for ECR
    docker tag $APP_NAME:$IMAGE_TAG $REGISTRY/$APP_NAME:$IMAGE_TAG
    docker tag $APP_NAME:$IMAGE_TAG $REGISTRY/$APP_NAME:latest
    
    # Login to ECR
    log "Logging into ECR..."
    aws ecr get-login-password --region $REGION | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin $REGISTRY
    
    # Push images
    log "Pushing images to ECR..."
    docker push $REGISTRY/$APP_NAME:$IMAGE_TAG
    docker push $REGISTRY/$APP_NAME:latest
    
    log "Image pushed successfully: $REGISTRY/$APP_NAME:$IMAGE_TAG"
}

# Deploy to Kubernetes
deploy_to_k8s() {
    log "Deploying to Kubernetes..."
    
    # Update kubeconfig
    aws eks update-kubeconfig --region $REGION --name $CLUSTER_NAME
    
    # Create namespace if it doesn't exist
    kubectl create namespace $NAMESPACE --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
    
    # Update image in deployment
    kubectl set image deployment/$APP_NAME web-app=$REGISTRY/$APP_NAME:$IMAGE_TAG -n $NAMESPACE
    
    # Wait for rollout to complete
    kubectl rollout status deployment/$APP_NAME -n $NAMESPACE --timeout=300s
    
    # Verify deployment
    kubectl get pods -n $NAMESPACE -l app=$APP_NAME
    
    log "Deployment completed successfully"
}

# Health check
health_check() {
    log "Performing health check..."
    
    # Get service endpoint
    SERVICE_IP=$(kubectl get service $APP_NAME-service -n $NAMESPACE -o jsonpath='{.status.loadBalancer.ingress[0].ip}' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    
    if [[ -z "$SERVICE_IP" ]]; then
        warn "LoadBalancer IP not yet assigned, checking pod health directly"
        
        # Check if pods are ready
        READY_PODS=$(kubectl get pods -n $NAMESPACE -l app=$APP_NAME -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.conditions[?(@.type=="Ready")].status}' | grep -o "True" | wc -l)
        TOTAL_PODS=$(kubectl get pods -n $NAMESPACE -l app=$APP_NAME --no-headers | wc -l)
        
        if [[ $READY_PODS -eq $TOTAL_PODS && $TOTAL_PODS -gt 0 ]]; then
            log "All $TOTAL_PODS pods are ready"
        else
            error "Only $READY_PODS out of $TOTAL_PODS pods are ready"
            exit 1
        fi
    else
        log "Service available at: $SERVICE_IP"
    fi
}

# Rollback function
rollback() {
    warn "Rolling back deployment..."
    kubectl rollout undo deployment/$APP_NAME -n $NAMESPACE
    kubectl rollout status deployment/$APP_NAME -n $NAMESPACE --timeout=300s
    log "Rollback completed"
}

# Main execution
main() {
    log "Starting deployment pipeline..."
    
    check_dependencies
    
    # Build and push if not in rollback mode
    if [[ "${1:-}" != "rollback" ]]; then
        build_and_push
    fi
    
    # Deploy or rollback
    if [[ "${1:-}" == "rollback" ]]; then
        rollback
    else
        deploy_to_k8s
    fi
    
    health_check
    
    log "Pipeline completed successfully!"
}

# Error handling
trap 'error "Script failed on line $LINENO"' ERR

# Run main function
main "$@"
